title: Pour-over at home, without the gooseneck
summary: A V60 recipe that survives a kitchen kettle, a supermarket scale and a distracted Tuesday morning.
body:
Every recipe we hand out at the counter assumes a gooseneck kettle and a scale that reads to a tenth of a gram. Almost nobody's kitchen has either, so here is the version that works in yours.

- 18 g of coffee, ground a little coarser than you think.
- 300 g of water, off the boil for thirty seconds.
- Two pours: 60 g to wet it, the rest in one slow go at forty seconds.

A blunt kettle pours faster than a gooseneck, which means the bed churns and the brew runs quick. Coarsen the grind one notch and you have it back. If that sentence meant nothing to you, start with [grind size is the dial](/blog/grind-size-is-the-dial/) and come back.

The whole thing takes two minutes and forgives being interrupted, which is the only test a home recipe ever has to pass.
